subject: Your password expires today
body: Your mailbox password expires in 2 hours. Click this link and sign in to keep your account active, or your email will be suspended.
explanation: Urgency plus a link asking for credentials is a common phishing pattern. One way to check: contact IT through a channel you already know, not the link.

subject: Team meeting moved to Thursday
body: Hi all, this week's team meeting moves to Thursday at 10:00 in the warehouse office. Same agenda as before, nothing to prepare.
explanation: It comes from a known colleague's usual address, asks for nothing, contains no link or attachment and matches something you'd expect. Not every email is a threat.

subject: Overdue invoice #20931 - payment needed today
body: Our records show an unpaid invoice for your book order. Please open the attached file, enable editing, and pay today to avoid a late fee.
explanation: An unexpected invoice from a sender you don't work with, an attachment that asks you to 'enable editing' and pressure to act today are classic malware tricks. Check with the finance team before opening anything.

subject: Quick favour, are you at your desk?
body: I'm in a meeting and can't talk. I need you to buy five gift cards for a supplier and send me the codes. I'll pay you back this afternoon.
explanation: This is a classic impersonation scam: a boss's name on an outside address, secrecy, urgency and gift cards. Call the person on a number you already have before doing anything.

subject: New order received: 3 items
body: A new order has been placed. Sign in to the web shop admin as you normally do to view and pack it. This message contains no links.
explanation: This matches the shop's usual notification, comes from the shop's own address and tells you to sign in the way you normally do, not through a link.
